Heidelberg Synagogue

Synagogue · Heidelberg, Germany

The current synagogue of the Jüdische Kultusgemeinde Heidelberg was built between 1992 and 1994 on the site of the former Villa Julius in the Weststadt district, replacing a series of postwar prayer rooms used since the community's re-establishment in 1945. Designed by architect Alfred Jacoby around a circular prayer hall at the center of a composition of geometric volumes, the building opened in January 1994 with support from the city of Heidelberg and the state of Baden-Württemberg. It houses the community's synagogue and adjoining center, and since 2016 its foyer has displayed a memorial wall of photographs documenting Stolpersteine placed throughout Heidelberg.
